video_title: Olivia Miles Is The WNBA's Best New Thinker

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on the mental challenge of dealing with public criticism
quotes.excerpt: It's so hard. Sometimes I just want to reply, and I'm like, 'Olivia, please don't get.'
quotes.quote: It's so hard. Sometimes I just want to reply, and I'm like, 'Olivia, please don't get.' Because it's not worth it. They have nothing to lose, we have everything to lose on our end. It's so hard to sit there and be like, 'This is not true,' or 'You have no idea what you're talking about.'

quotes.speaker: Tommy Alter
quotes.summary_phrase: Tommy Alter and Olivia Miles on the 'Strayzand Effect' of social media replies
quotes.excerpt: Your reply, it's the Strayzand effect. Your reply makes it a thing. It makes it a story.

text_blocks.speaker: Tommy Alter
text_blocks.text: And your reply, it's the Strayzand effect. Your reply makes it a thing. It makes it a story.

text_blocks.speaker: Olivia Miles
text_blocks.text: Of course. Exactly. It makes it a story.

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on building professional habits at TCU
quotes.excerpt: I think it's a good routine that I built at TCU this past year, making sure I had
quotes.quote: I think it's a good routine that I built at TCU this past year, making sure I had pro-level habits, whether that's my routine, what I'm eating, how much I'm sleeping. I like to journal and meditate. I'm a very spiritual person, so I stick to good habits that keep me stress-free.

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on learning from WNBA veterans and watching film
quotes.excerpt: I have Hall of Famers on staff who've done it and have played against the Diana Taurasis
quotes.quote: I have Hall of Famers on staff who've done it and have played against the Diana Taurasis, the Sue Birds, the Maya Moores, and they know what it takes day in and day out. I think it's leaning on people around me, watching a lot of film, preparing. Once you play teams over and over, you start to get tendencies and you start to get a feel for the game.

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on her transition from soccer to basketball
quotes.excerpt: Basketball was the most fun to me. I love soccer, but in a different way.
quotes.quote: Basketball was the most fun to me. I love soccer, but in a different way. I think basketball is more chaotic and more fun and fast-paced. It was eighth grade when I realized I could be good, but high school I was like, 'Yeah, this is it, I'm going to take this all the way.'

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on how her parents' engineering background influenced her game
quotes.excerpt: My dad has always stressed to my brother and I just to be high academic.
quotes.quote: My dad has always stressed to my brother and I just to be high academic. He was always honest about our grades. He never really held our hand through things. He always made us critically think about things and problem-solve, and I think it's translated really well to sports. As a point guard, you got to figure out different things and learn how to quickly solve situations and read certain problems.

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on the players she grew up watching
quotes.excerpt: I watched the Jason Williams, the Jason Kidds, Steve Nash, Stephen Curry, all those guys.
quotes.quote: I watched the Jason Williams, the Jason Kidds, Steve Nash, Stephen Curry, all those guys. I forgot to mention Kyrie. Kyrie was a big influence, obviously, Jersey kid. Watching what they do, wanting to do crazy layups like that and handles, and obviously Steve Nash's passing. As a student of the game, you just love to learn things and pick up different things.

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on developing her court vision and anticipation
quotes.excerpt: I always had a different instinct seeing things, seeing space, reading situations, reading windows, timing.
quotes.quote: I always had a different instinct seeing things, seeing space, reading situations, reading windows, timing. It's definitely developed over time, practice and reps. And watching film has helped a lot. But I also would attribute a lot of that to soccer, like the windows and anticipation and leading people places.

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on her hunger to keep learning and improving
quotes.excerpt: I'm always learning and never satisfied with what I'm doing.
quotes.quote: I'm always learning and never satisfied with what I'm doing. That doesn't mean I'm not grateful to be where I'm at, but I'm just hungry to learn more and to be better in every situation.

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on using data and film to improve her game
quotes.excerpt: There's so much data now, and there's like sensors in every arena, and it tells you very specific things.
quotes.quote: There's so much data now, and there's like sensors in every arena, and it tells you very specific things that you can track. I can see, for example, that a certain shot goes a lower percentage going right than going left. It's little stuff like that that you can kind of pick up the tendencies easier than before.

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on her friendship with Sonia Citron
quotes.excerpt: Sonia and I decided to go to college together. We've been friends for a really long time.
quotes.quote: Sonia and I decided to go to college together. We've been friends for a really long time. To make it this far, and then to have the success that we're having is so rare. So it's definitely something that we acknowledge, and we'll always have a friendship just because we went into college together and spent so many years at Notre Dame together.

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on her ability to adapt quickly to new environments
quotes.excerpt: I didn't have time to sit there and overthink things. I literally just had to go in, play.
quotes.quote: I didn't have time to sit there and overthink things. I literally just had to go in, play, and figure things out on the fly, which I'm usually pretty good at. So the timing definitely favored the way that I go about things, and it's helped me.

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on the challenge of guarding Kelsey Mitchell
quotes.excerpt: We played the Fever the first time and Kelsey Mitchell was just killing us.
quotes.quote: We played the Fever the first time and Kelsey Mitchell was just killing us. She was killing us, and I was like, 'Yeah, she can't be guarded.' That definitely was a 'welcome to the league' moment where I was like, 'Damn, this is legit.'

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on the difficulty of guarding efficient players like Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers
quotes.excerpt: Obviously Caitlin with the shooting and her playmaking ability. She's so good with her right hand attacking downhill.
quotes.quote: Obviously Caitlin with the shooting and her playmaking ability. She's so good with her right hand attacking downhill and creating for others. And in transition, she's deadly. It is annoying to play against her, right? You got to guard her and you got to make sure that you have bodies on her at all times. And same for Paige. Paige is great to her right hand and great posting up in the short corner and facilitating for her teammates as well.

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on Chelsea Gray's surgical playmaking
quotes.excerpt: She's a different type of player, but she still can't be guarded. She's surgical.
quotes.quote: She's a different type of player, but she still can't be guarded. She's surgical. The timing and her knowing where her teammates are going to be before they do. I feel like we have a lot of similarities in that way, our processing.

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on the longevity and winning mindset of legends like LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: To have the longevity that they have and to win as well is so unheard of.
quotes.quote: To have the longevity that they have and to win as well is so unheard of. It's so aspiring. I don't think I want to play for that long, but basketball is such a love of mine that I want to give it all I have and learn from the greats.

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on playing with a 'carefree' mindset
quotes.excerpt: I'm happy that I played carefree, because that was a stride for me in college.
quotes.quote: I'm happy that I played carefree, because that was a stride for me in college. I carried too much weight of things that didn't matter and overthinking, overanalyzing. So I'm happy that I played carefree and really leaned into my teammates and the people around me.

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on how she approaches player development
quotes.excerpt: I was drilling her with questions and she was like, 'Ba, ba, ba.' She just knew exactly.
quotes.quote: I was drilling her with questions and she was like, 'Ba, ba, ba.' She just knew exactly what she was talking about. When you're around someone who's like-minded and thinks the game the way you do, it's like she understands it. What I've been most impressed with with her is figuring out how to get the best out of her players.

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on Courtney Williams' leadership style
quotes.excerpt: Court has just a way about her to not take things too seriously in the best way.
quotes.quote: Court has just a way about her to not take things too seriously in the best way. But she has a way about her where, for example, after a loss, she's like, 'Flush it, like let's go, you're still you.' She still allows me to laugh in those moments, and I cherish that bond I have with her so much and just cheering her on.

quotes.speaker: Olivia Miles
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles on ignoring external criticism
quotes.excerpt: You shouldn't take criticism from someone you wouldn't take advice from.
quotes.quote: What I heard was, you shouldn't take criticism from someone you wouldn't take advice from. That's kind of stuck with me because it's just true. You shouldn't pay attention to people that really have and hold no value over you and who are saying things that are clearly not true, but obviously hurt for some reason.
